final_candidates.decision_summary: Top ESM-1v plausibility with nonzero F frequency among homologs at a GP1 epitope-adjacent surface position; bulky aromatic substitution plausibly disrupts Arevirumab-3 binding while remaining structurally tolerated.
Surface-helix position in GP1 where a charge/polarity change could perturb antibody recognition; ESM-1v neutral-to-favorable though N is not observed in homologs, keeping confidence moderate.
Best MSA tolerance in the pool (A ~12%) plus solid ESM plausibility; conservative substitution in a GP1 surface region offering modest escape potential with low viability risk.

stop_reason.detail: Phenotype evidence is non-applicable for all candidates and remaining priors yield a stable Top-3, so additional tool calls would not change the decision.

history.rationale: Surface-exposed GP1 residue in the nAb contact region; bulky hydrophobic substitution is a classic escape route at glycan-adjacent epitopes with moderate conservation.
Phenotype tool returned not_applicable; no evidence against. S155 is in the GP1 glycan-shield region implicated in Arevirumab-3 epitopes, so the hypothesis stands.
Top ESM-1v plausibility (1.0) and nonzero F frequency in homologs at a conserved GP1 epitope-adjacent position; strong combined prior support.
GP1 loop residue near the Arevirumab epitope cluster; charge-flip at a surface Asn can disrupt antibody binding while minimally affecting folding.
No new evidence; N-glycan-site disruption near the GP1 apex could remove shielding but alter antibody contacts — retains value pending MSA/PLM evidence.
ESM-1v strongly disfavors (0.29) and D never seen in homologs; demoted despite glycosylation-site escape rationale.
GP1 surface residue likely within or near nAb footprints; subtle substitution preserving polarity should retain function while reducing binding.
No new evidence; surface-exposed GP1 residue plausibly within neutralizing epitopes.
ESM-1v neutral (1.0), but N never observed among homologs at 170; surface helix position plausibly alters antibody binding.
GP1 surface threonine near epitope region; conservative change that may weaken antibody contacts without harming entry.
No new evidence; GP1 surface residue candidate for epitope disruption.
Best MSA tolerance in the pool (A at 12%) plus solid ESM (0.60); conservative substitution in GP1 surface region.
Alternative at the same GP1 hotspot as S155F; smaller side chain offers escape via loss of key polar contact with lower folding risk.
Conservative alternative at the same site as S155F; kept as lower-risk fallback pending evidence.
Decent ESM plausibility (0.77) at the same epitope-relevant position 155; kept as fallback to S155F.
Conservative variant at the same GP1 epitope residue; escape through altered hydrogen-bond geometry.
Glycan-site alternative to N119D; retained for comparison.
Removes the N119 glycan (escape mechanism preserved) with better evolutionary tolerance (S at 9%) than N119D, though ESM is lukewarm.
Surface lysine on GP1; charge reversal could disrupt electrostatic antibody engagement while remaining on the solvent-exposed face.
Charge-swap could disrupt antibody binding, but without phenotype data its risk of impairing entry rises; slightly downranked.
ESM-1v neutral (1.0) and charge reversal at a surface-exposed G1 beta-strand could strongly disrupt antibody binding; MSA coverage lower but nonzero tolerance.
Surface acidic residue; neutralizing the charge may reduce nAb affinity with low structural cost.
No new evidence; mild change at surface residue.
High ESM plausibility (0.97) and 11% N frequency among homologs; charge removal in helix region could perturb epitope geometry.
GP1 hydrophobic surface residue; aromatic substitution could remodel the epitope surface while packing compatibly.
Hydrophobic-to-aromatic change may perturb local packing; downranked pending structural evidence.
F never observed among homologs and only moderate ESM support (0.56); weakest overall evidence profile in the pool.

history.rationale: GP1 surface histidine adjacent to the proposed epitope cluster; loss of imidazole contacts may impair antibody binding.

ESM-1v neutral (1.0) with modest MSA tolerance (4%); surface helix position remains a plausible escape site.
